elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Amended 16.2 reads "Array shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless each of Ono, its Affiliates and Sublicensees...", and the inserted IP sentence repeats "Array shall defend and indemnify the Ono Indemnitees". "Defend" is now express and runs to Ono and its Affiliates (and Sublicensees).

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Retained 16.2 chapeau: "Array shall ... indemnify and hold harmless each of Ono, its Affiliates and Sublicensees ... from and against any and all Liabilities from any Third Party Claims incurred by any Ono Indemnitee".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "Notwithstanding Section 11.4, Array shall defend and indemnify the Ono Indemnitees against any Third Party Claim alleging that any Product, or any deliverable or service supplied by Array hereunder, infringes or misappropriates the intellectual property rights of a Third Party." Products are the contract's deliverable analogue, and the targeted override neutralises the "own expense" allocation in Section 11.4.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: New head 16.2(e): "Array's breach of applicable Law".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: New head 16.2(f): "any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Ono's Confidential Information caused by Array". Confidential Information is the agreement's defined category for Ono-supplied/held information, so this is the correct local analogue of Customer Data.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: New head 16.2(g): "Array's gross negligence or willful misconduct"; the retained tail excepts only claims resulting from an Ono Indemnitee's gross negligence or wilful misconduct, so there is no contradiction.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: Unamended 16.3: Indemnitee "shall promptly notify the other Party (the 'Indemnitor') in writing of any Third Party Claim".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: Unamended 16.3: "the Indemnitor shall have sole control of the defense and/or settlement thereof", subject to keeping the Indemnitee informed and settlement-consent limits.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: Unamended 16.3: "The Indemnitee ... shall cooperate fully with the Indemnitor and its legal representatives in the investigation of any action with respect to a Third Party Claim".

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: 16.1 is rewritten to only "(a) materials, data or content provided by Ono to Array under this Agreement; and (b) Ono's breach of applicable Law"; the former product-liability, clinical-study and Article 15 prongs are deleted.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: The inserted sentence in 16.2 gives an express Array defence/indemnity for Third Party Claims alleging infringement or misappropriation of Third Party intellectual property rights.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: the inserted IP indemnity contains no Ono-modification exclusion. Omission of a permitted vendor carve-out does not defeat the element and is more favourable to us.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no combination carve-out is included; its absence broadens our protection and does not defeat the checklist item.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no Ono-specification carve-out is included; absence is customer-favourable.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: Neither the inserted IP sentence nor Article 16 contains any procure/modify/replace remedy obligation on Array; no such operative language appears anywhere in the rendered text.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund-of-fees (or of upfront/milestone payments) mechanic is added or retained if the mitigation remedies are unavailable.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3x annual fees super-cap is stated in the rendered language; the indemnity is uncapped on its face (a customer-favourable gap, but the fallback element is literally unsatisfied).

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all ten preferred elements are met on the operative language (defence duty, indemnitee scope, new IP infringement head, breach of Law, unauthorised access/disclosure of Ono Confidential Information, gross negligence/wilful misconduct, plus the unamended 16.3 notice / sole control / full cooperation procedure and a narrowed 16.1).

Fallback level is not complete (no procure-modify-replace remedy, no refund fallback, no 3x super-cap), but that is immaterial because the preferred checklist is fully satisfied; the two missing vendor-protective items would only narrow our recovery.

Minimality holds: the edits touch only 16.1 (narrowing our indemnity, required by the tenth preferred element) and 16.2 (defence duty plus heads (e)-(g) and the IP sentence). Section 16.3 is left untouched and Array's existing product-liability/clinical-study/Article 15 prongs are retained. No survival tail, expense language, extra damages categories or boilerplate was added.

The "Notwithstanding Section 11.4" opener is narrow and targeted rather than a blanket override; it is needed to stop the retained "at its own expense" Infringement Action allocation contradicting the new IP indemnity, so it preserves intent rather than creating a dangling conflict.

Minor drafting point (not a failure): 16.2 now says "defend, indemnify and hold harmless" in the chapeau and the inserted sentence repeats "defend and indemnify". Consider folding the IP head into the (b)-(g) enumeration as a new clause (h) with the Section 11.4 carve-out attached, to avoid a duplicated defence formulation.

Watch-item for the drafter: 16.2 continues to open at "(b)" because prong (a) sits in an uncited paragraph; confirm on the full text that the lettering still runs (a) through (g) after insertion, and that no other provision (e.g. insurance or Article 15 cross-references) points to the deleted 16.1(a)-(d) prongs.

If Array resists, the natural trade is to restore the reciprocal product-liability and clinical-study allocation in 16.1 in exchange for keeping the IP indemnity, as the margin comment already offers.
